title: Add canonical generator identity and bounded Siemens name policy
goal: Replace the oversized pre-publication GEN-VALVE-FOUNDATION-001 implementation attempt with a first small foundation slice: add deterministic parsed-model input identity in the vendor-neutral compiler boundary and the minimal Siemens emitted-name/symbol policy in SiemensBackend, with focused tests. Do not implement manifest/output/CLI profile plumbing yet and do not introduce any unverified Valve contract fact.

baselineEvidence.failedRun: Autonomous Agent run 36250733507 (#27) failed before publication on both attempt 1 and attempt 2. No candidate PR was created and repair budget was not consumed.
baselineEvidence.attempt1: The coding step hit its step limit before self-test; deterministic acceptance found duplicate GeneratorManifest.SchemaVersion plus unresolved DiagnosticCode references.
baselineEvidence.attempt2: A fresh rerun again hit its step limit before self-test; deterministic acceptance found CS7036 in the disposable CanonicalIdentity implementation. Publication was skipped.
baselineEvidence.decompositionReason: Two independent pre-publication attempts show the combined identity+name+manifest+containment+CLI+diagnostics task is too broad for the current bounded coder step budget. Split by architecture boundary rather than increasing runtime limits.

scope: Add one small vendor-neutral canonical input identity helper in PlcCompiler. It may consume the normalized parsed AutomationDevice model from Domain, but Domain itself must not change.

The input identity must be a lowercase SHA-256 over a deterministic canonical representation of the parsed model. Include device name plus every field name/type in original order. Do not sort fields, do not include an opaque profile token, raw JSON whitespace/property order, file paths, timestamps, locale, machine/user identity or output location.

Add the smallest Siemens emitted-name/symbol policy in SiemensBackend only. Reject null/empty names, names that cannot be safely emitted by the current quoted UDT/type/field generator policy, and case-insensitive duplicate allocated field symbols. Use stable bounded diagnostic codes or typed error identity; do not silently rename.

Integrate that policy into SclDataTypeGenerator before emitting a UDT. Keep the policy deliberately bounded to names the current generator emits; do not claim complete Siemens/TIA identifier semantics or add a catalog/framework.

Add focused tests for canonical identity equality for equivalent parsed models, order sensitivity, name/type sensitivity, invalid/empty names, case-insensitive duplicates, and existing Motor/Time SCL regression.
Do not modify GeneratorCli, manifest/output-containment behavior, TiaV21Worker, workflows, tasks, agents, vendor payloads, runner configuration or IndustrialMDE in the implementation candidate.
Do not add fbValve_Solenoid parameters, dependencies, versions, DB/ownership/memory/target facts or any Valve call.

requirements: Candidate changes are limited exactly to candidatePolicy.allowedPaths; Domain remains unchanged and vendor-neutral.
Canonical input identity is deterministic lowercase SHA-256 derived from the normalized parsed AutomationDevice only; it has no profile-token or environment/path dependency.
Two independently constructed AutomationDevice instances with identical device name and ordered fields produce the same identity; changing a field name/type or field order changes identity.
The identity implementation preserves field declaration order and does not sort fields for hashing.
Siemens-specific emitted-name/symbol policy exists only in SiemensBackend and is invoked by SclDataTypeGenerator before output.
Null/empty or unsupported emitted names and case-insensitive duplicate field symbols fail with stable bounded diagnostic identity; user names are not silently renamed.
Focused Linux tests cover the identity and name-policy cases and all existing SiemensBackend tests remain green.
Existing Motor and Time UDT generation remains compatible.
No GeneratorCli/manifest/output-containment implementation is added in this slice.
No unqualified Valve contract fact is asserted in code/tests/examples.
